contract: The candidate calls Muxer::new and write_picture for every authored picture, then polls TransportStream to logical EOF over the resulting TS188 bytes. The reference demuxes those same muxed bytes with the pinned FFmpeg 9.0.2 decode profile's MPEG-TS demuxer and +noparse+nofillin.

Each case supplies default or decimal TSID, ONID, program, PMT PID, video PID and stream type followed by provider and service names. Each input picture has big-endian signed 64-bit PTS and DTS in 90 kHz ticks, a one-byte key indicator, a big-endian 32-bit payload length and the coded picture bytes.

Packet rows (kind 1) fold PID, optional PTS and DTS, flags, first carrier offset and payload length and all payload bytes, in order. Candidate clocks are raw period-zero PES values. Bit 0 compares the transport random-access indicator. On the reference side, read this bit at the demuxed packet position after verifying the TS sync, PID and payload start. Other public packet flags still compare.

After draining, catalogue rows (kind 5) fold the program number and PMT PID, each stream PID and tag, then the provider and service tags with presence, length and bytes. The candidate reads the names from the emitted SDT service descriptor. A clean EOF adds kind 7.

Check the candidate's original wire against each input picture. Require SDT at 45,000 DTS ticks, PAT and PMT at 9,000 ticks or at a transition to a key picture, initial tables in SDT/PAT/PMT order, per-PID continuity, and exact section CRC and stuffing. Check first-carrier PCR and random access, unbounded video PES headers, both coded timestamps and every coded picture byte across all its carriers.

A refused MuxConfig emits one kind 8 row. When the candidate supplies no TS, the reference runs its own muxer against the same configuration. Header refusal with zero output emits kind 8. Successful TS output emits kind 9. The refusal cases cover zero program number, reserved or colliding PIDs, unsupported stream type, non-printable or non-ASCII names, and both name length and combined SDT capacity.
pin_note: Pins are recorded by transport-views manifest --record from the decode demuxer for read-back and its muxer for configuration admission.

open_deviations.reading: A writer configured for MPEG-1/2 video refuses AVC
open_deviations.clause: H.222.0 §2.4.4.10 Table 2-34 assigns stream type 0x1B to AVC. MuxConfig limits its writer to types 0x01 and 0x02.
open_deviations.candidate: Refuses the AVC configuration before writing carriers.
open_deviations.reference: Admits AVC and emits TS188 with stream type 0x1B.

open_deviations.reading: The provider name contains a tab
open_deviations.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 §6.2.33 and Annex A §A.1 define the service text layout and permitted control codes. MuxConfig admits printable ASCII.
open_deviations.candidate: Refuses the provider name before writing carriers.
open_deviations.reference: Accepts the tab in the provider field and emits TS188.

open_deviations.reading: The service name requires a non-ASCII character
open_deviations.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 §6.2.33 and Annex A §A.2 provide alternative text encodings. MuxConfig admits printable ASCII.
open_deviations.reference: Admits the non-ASCII service name and emits TS188.

open_deviations.reading: The names together exceed one SDT carrier
open_deviations.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 §§5.1.2 and 6.2.33 permit a section across carriers. MuxConfig limits the names to 158 combined bytes so the SDT fits one carrier.
open_deviations.candidate: Refuses the 159-byte combined names before writing carriers.
open_deviations.reference: Admits both names and emits TS188 using a second SDT carrier.
